layout_notes: Zones in this guide are keyed to the REAL turn numbers 1-9. They bind to the Big Willow layout profile by lap length (~4,023 m) via the coach's layout-aware guide loading (v2.17.0) -- but the zone NUMBERS only match your driving once your detected corner map for this layout is checked against them. If detection merges or splits a corner, this guide gets re-keyed, the same drill as corner naming.

Olsen teaches the track in six pieces: Turn 1, Turn 2, Turns 3-4 as a pair, Turns 5-6 as a pair, Turn 8, Turn 9 (Turn 7 is a kink). The through-line of the lap: the uphill 3-4 section is a sacrifice, and from the exit of Turn 5 you are effectively flat all the way to the braking zone for Turn 9.

The video is from 2012 and Big Willow has been resurfaced since -- painted cone marks and other surface references from the video may not exist on the current track, and the mod may model either era. The line and the technique carry over; treat specific marks as approximate until you've seen the corner in the sim.

source.layout_note: The DE / time-trial line Olsen teaches at Willow Springs International Raceway (Big Willow), all nine corners. Speeds quoted are for his car -- scale to yours. Landmarks he teaches by (Budweiser wall lettering, the white water tower, painted cone marks) are real-track features; the DDM mod models the circuit but may not carry every sign.
source.title: My corner-by-corner guide to Willow Springs Raceway

1.character: High-speed left, 70-90 mph in Olsen's car, with a BLIND exit hidden by a rise and drop -- which is why novices brake far more than the corner needs. Brake in a straight line on the right, downshift before a not-especially-late turn-in, and be back on the throttle BEFORE the apex, which sits where the row of reflectors begins on the left. No late or trail braking here: brake early, downshift, turn in, get on the gas, and let the car run out to the right on exit -- pinching it tight is the common mistake. A variant entry leaves a car width unused on the right for a smoother ride over the surface irregularities, and a slightly early turn-in can work, but early-apexing runs you off into a bumpy infield.
1.name: Turn 1

tips.text: The exit is blind, but this is a 70-90 mph corner -- brake early and straight on the right, then commit. Over-braking for what you can't see is the novice tell here.
Be back on the throttle before the apex, where the reflectors start on the left, and let the car run out to the right -- don't pinch the exit.

2.character: A long, high-speed right sweeper, 80-100 mph, usually driven as a double apex but better understood as one very late single apex. Enter from full left, but never go further left than mid-track in the first half -- the outside collects marbles and just makes the track longer. The speed throws you left around mid-corner; from there you steer the car with the THROTTLE, bringing it gradually right to the very late apex. Miss that apex and the car gets thrown all the way left on exit, where going off is scary. Advanced option in light cars: dive in early, let the car drift to scrub speed, and skip braking entirely -- worth a few tenths, not for every car or driver.
2.name: Turn 2

tips.text: This corner is steered with the throttle -- hold your line inside mid-track early, then feed power to bring the car right to the very late apex.
The apex here is later than it looks -- the entry half is positioning. If you apex early you'll be thrown left on exit with nowhere to go.

3.character: The hardest braking on the track, into a slow uphill left. Get ALL the braking and the downshift finished before turn-in -- there is very little to gain carrying speed in and a lot to lose turning in early, and trail braking does not pay here. Go deep into the right side of the entrance and turn in late; a small white mark on the right, well into the curve, shows where you want to be before turning. Camber changes at the exit make the car hard to settle, and the exit is where novices go off. Treat everything from this braking zone to the throttle point out of Turn 4 as one sacrifice: you're setting up the downhill, not making time uphill.
3.name: Turn 3

tips.text: Hardest stop on the track -- get braking and downshift completely done before turn-in, and don't trail brake it.
Turn in late: go deep to the right at the entrance, past the white mark. Early turn-in is where the time -- and the exit offs -- come from.

4.character: The top of the hill, paired with Turn 3 as a single sacrifice section. Exit 3 and drive straight up the hill -- the rumble strip you pass on the right is NOT an apex, and the track starts turning long before you do (Olsen aims students at the 'B' in the Budweiser wall lettering). Enter Turn 4 much further LEFT than instinct suggests, keeping the widest possible arc over the slowest point of the lap; two red cone marks on the left set it up -- parallel with the track edge at the first, turning right toward the late apex at the second. Lift, rotate at the top, point at the apex by the corner-worker station, then full throttle down the hill. The front-right tire can clip the dirt at the apex on a car that's lifting that wheel anyway. If you brake for 4 at all, it's the one corner that rewards braking very late.
4.name: Turn 4

tips.text: The whole 3-4 climb is a sacrifice -- rotate once at the top and get to full throttle for the downhill. Time is made on this exit, not on the way up.
Stay left and keep the arc wide -- enter Turn 4 much further left than feels natural, and don't chase the rumble strip on the right out of 3; it isn't an apex.

5.character: A left with a downhill entrance and uphill exit, and the gateway to the fast half of the lap. From full left out of 4, bring the car back right and brake parallel with the candy-stripe rumble strip on the right. Brake and turn in EARLY -- the surface gets more slippery the deeper you go into the corner. No downshift: most cars hold one gear from the entrance of 3 all the way to the uphill of 6. The entire point of the corner is the earliest possible full throttle, because from here you are flat -- past 6, past 7, through 8 -- until the braking zone for 9. Olsen's own tip: brake even earlier than the downhill speed makes you want to; carrying speed in sets up a spectacular save, not a lap time. Exit as close to mid-track as you can.
5.name: Turn 5

tips.text: Brake earlier than the downhill run tempts you to, alongside the candy-stripe on the right, and turn in early -- grip gets worse the deeper you go here.
Get to full throttle as early as you possibly can -- you're flat from this exit all the way to the braking zone for Turn 9.

6.character: The right-hander over the hill after 5. Turn in late and hug the right-side rumble strip to take the drama out of cresting the hill mid-corner. Don't upshift at the very top of the hill -- short-shift on the way up, or hold the shift until the car is settled and heading downhill toward 7.
6.name: Turn 6

tips.text: Turn in late and hug the right rumble strip over the crest -- and don't grab the upshift at the very top; short-shift early or wait until the car settles downhill.

7.character: A kink Olsen tells students to ignore entirely -- the only thought here is carrying maximum speed toward Turn 8.
7.name: Turn 7

tips.text: Don't coach yourself through this one -- it's a kink. Everything here is about arriving at Turn 8 as fast as possible.

8.character: One of the fastest corners on any track anywhere. Most cars don't brake at all and many are flat on the gas -- in Olsen's telling, many cars should be flat from the exit of Turn 5 all the way through here. Dive toward the inside as early as you can and ride the inside edge: the washboard bumps are worst mid-track. The apex is very late (there's a red mark for it, but you won't be looking at the track at that speed). His reassurance: for all its speed, people very rarely go off here -- the corner holds more speed than your brain first accepts.
8.name: Turn 8

tips.text: If you're lifting here, that lift is the lap time -- most cars are flat. Ride the inside where the washboard bumps are smaller and commit to the very late apex.
Get to the inside early and stay there -- the bumps live mid-track, and this corner holds far more speed than it feels like it should.

9.character: The famous one: a decreasing-radius right that scares drivers more the faster they get. The first half takes speed easily, the second half doesn't -- so a late turn-in is essential. Exit 8 around mid-track and brake moderately on the short straight once the car is settled. Then the landmarks do the work: spot the building near the track entrance on the horizon and begin a SLOW drift from mid-track toward the left edge; the white water tower is the key reference -- drive toward it and let your line to the tower choose your path and your turning point. Turn in around the middle of the three red cone marks on the left edge. There is almost always a cone at the apex and you do not want to miss it by much; done right, the car gets drawn down into a low spot at the apex -- feel that dip and the exit will take care of itself, at 80-100 mph past the cone, using as much of the left as you need.
9.name: Turn 9

tips.text: Decreasing radius means the early turn-in is the trap -- exit 8 at mid-track, drift left slowly on the line to the white water tower, and turn in late, around the middle red mark.
Do the braking moderately on the short straight after 8, once the car is settled -- then let the tower line set the corner, and don't miss the apex cone.
